views.name: race_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  year,
  round,
  circuit_id,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  url,
  fp1_date,
  fp1_time,
  fp2_date,
  fp2_time,
  fp3_date,
  fp3_time,
  quali_date,
  quali_time,
  sprint_date,
  sprint_time,
  CAST(date AS TEXT) AS date_text
FROM races

params.description: Provides one-row-per-race basic metadata (identifiers, schedule, and URLs) for races.
params.when_to_use: Look up race attributes (name, circuit, date/time, URLs) by race_id or by year/round. | Compose reports that need race-level context for results, lap times, qualifying, or pit stop aggregations. | Filter or join datasets to restrict analysis to a specific race or set of races before aggregating measures.
params.output_schema: race_id: unique identifier for the race (derived from races.race_id) | year: season year the race belongs to (derived from races.year) | round: round number within the season (derived from races.round) | circuit_id: identifier of the circuit where the race was held (derived from races.circuit_id) | name: official race name (derived from races.name) | date: scheduled race date (derived from races.date) | time: scheduled race start time (derived from races.time) | url: reference URL for the race entry (derived from races.url) | fp1_date: first practice 1 date (derived from races.fp1_date) | fp1_time: first practice 1 time (derived from races.fp1_time) | fp2_date: first practice 2 date (derived from races.fp2_date) | fp2_time: first practice 2 time (derived from races.fp2_time) | fp3_date: first practice 3 date (derived from races.fp3_date) | fp3_time: first practice 3 time (derived from races.fp3_time) | quali_date: qualifying session date (derived from races.quali_date) | quali_time: qualifying session time (derived from races.quali_time) | sprint_date: sprint session date (derived from races.sprint_date) | sprint_time: sprint session time (derived from races.sprint_time) | date_text: text-cast of the race date (derived from CAST(races.date AS TEXT))
params.grounded_columns: races.race_id | races.year | races.round | races.circuit_id | races.name | races.date | races.time | races.url | races.fp1_date | races.fp1_time | races.fp2_date | races.fp2_time | races.fp3_date | races.fp3_time | races.quali_date | races.quali_time | races.sprint_date | races.sprint_time
params.metric: No aggregate metrics are defined in this view; all columns are direct projections from races (including date_text = CAST(races.date AS TEXT)).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_with_summary on circuit_id = circuit_id — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race and circuits_with_summary is one-row-per-circuit; joining will not duplicate race-level rows (many races can map to one circuit, but that does not multiply race rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on no direct key normally; if joining by driver_id you must aggregate driver-level measures first. Joining driver_dim (one-row-per-driver) to race_basic on no repeating race keys is safe only when you intend to produce a cross product (not recommended) — prefer joining race_basic to race_results which contains driver_id per race. | DO NOT directly join race_basic to one-to-many tables/views such as race_results, lap_times_per_driver, pit_stops_per_driver, qualifying_grid, or lap_times_running_stats without handling multiplicity, because those views/tables have multiple rows per race (e.g., many results or lap records per race) and will multiply any race-level measures if joined directly. Instead: | - To attach aggregated measures from a one-to-many source, first aggregate that source to one row per race_id (for example: race_results aggregated to counts, wins, or points per race_id), then join the aggregated result to race_basic on race_id. | - Or, when joining to race_results, perform analytics at the driver-result grain (one row per race_id + driver_id) and avoid interpreting race_basic's one-row-per-race columns as measures to be summed. | Example safe compositions: | - race_basic JOIN (SELECT race_id, COUNT(*) AS result_count FROM race_results GROUP BY race_id) USING (race_id) — safe because RHS is aggregated to one row per race_id. | - race_basic JOIN circuits_with_summary USING (circuit_id) — safe because both sides are at stable grains (race_basic: one row per race; circuits_with_summary: one row per circuit). | Reasoning about duplication: race_basic's rows are one-per-race (grain = race_id). Joins that preserve race_id as unique on the race_basic side (i.e., to one-row-per-race or one-row-per-circuit tables) will not duplicate. Joins to tables with multiple rows per race_id will duplicate race_basic rows unless the other side is pre-aggregated or the join includes additional keys to move to a finer grain (e.g., join to race_results on race_id AND driver_id produces one row per race+driver).

views.description: Normalized projection of races with canonical date/time fields and essential identifiers. Use this to join race metadata to results, lap times, pit stops, and standings. Keeps original column names and exposes a derived epoch_date for easy time-based ordering. | Use for: List races in a year or range; Join race metadata to results, lap_times, pit_stops; Filter races by session availability
counter_examples: Which constructors had the top 3 combined points from their best driver and team, and in which years did they achieve them?

views.name: driver_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driver_id,
  driver_ref,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url,
  (COALESCE(forename, '') || CASE WHEN forename IS NOT NULL AND surname IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(surname, '')) AS full_name
FROM drivers

params.description: Driver dimension with one row per driver, providing identifiers and basic personal attributes (name, nationality, DOB, URL) and a composed full_name.
params.when_to_use: Look up driver attributes (e.g., display driver name, code, nationality, DOB) when building reports or joins. | Join to race results, lap times, pit stops, qualifying, or championship/rankings to add driver descriptive fields. | Compose into aggregated analyses that need driver-level grouping keys (driver_id) and descriptive labels.
params.output_schema: driver_id: surrogate/primary key for a driver — sourced from drivers.driver_id | driver_ref: short unique reference for a driver — sourced from drivers.driver_ref | number: racing number for the driver (may be NULL) — sourced from drivers.number | code: short code (3-letter) for the driver (may be NULL) — sourced from drivers.code | forename: given name (may be NULL) — sourced from drivers.forename | surname: family name (may be NULL) — sourced from drivers.surname | dob: date of birth (may be NULL) — sourced from drivers.dob | nationality: nationality string (may be NULL) — sourced from drivers.nationality | url: URL to driver resource (may be NULL) — sourced from drivers.url | full_name: concatenation of forename and surname with a single space when both present; if one side is NULL the other is returned without extra space — derived expression: (COALESCE(forename, '') || CASE WHEN forename IS NOT NULL AND surname IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(surname, ''))
params.grounded_columns: drivers.driver_id | drivers.driver_ref | drivers.number | drivers.code | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.dob | drivers.nationality | drivers.url
params.metric: full_name = (COALESCE(drivers.forename, '') || CASE WHEN drivers.forename IS NOT NULL AND drivers.surname IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(drivers.surname, ''))  -- derived expression (non-aggregated)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on race_basic.driver_id = driver_dim.driver_id — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver and contains no aggregated measures; joining to a many-row event like race_basic will replicate driver rows in the result, but will not duplicate any driver-level measures since driver_dim contains no aggregates. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on constructor_dim.constructor_id = driver_dim.driver_id is NOT appropriate unless driver_id = constructor_id in your schema (do NOT join on unrelated keys). Instead join driver_dim to constructor_dim via an intermediate table (e.g., race_results) matching the correct keys. | do NOT join driver_dim directly to one-to-many fact views (race_results, lap_times_per_driver, pit_stops_per_driver, qualifying_grid, lap_times_running_stats) expecting aggregated driver measures to remain unchanged — these joins will multiply driver rows because those views have multiple rows per driver per event. If you need driver-level aggregates after joining to a one-to-many, either: | - aggregate the fact side first to one row per driver (e.g., SUM/COUNT grouped by driver_id) and then join to driver_dim, or | - perform the join and then re-aggregate at the driver_id grain to produce correct driver-level metrics. | safe composition examples: | - To display driver attributes for each race result row: join race_results ON race_results.driver_id = driver_dim.driver_id (this is safe for descriptive enrichment; any measures in race_results are at the race_result grain and not duplicated by driver_dim). | - To compute total laps by driver: aggregate lap_times_per_driver to SUM(laps) GROUP BY driver_id, then join to driver_dim ON driver_id — safe because the aggregation removes the one-to-many multiplicity before joining. | Notes on duplication: driver_dim itself contains no aggregated numeric metrics; therefore duplication concerns arise only when joining it to multi-row tables. The planner should ensure that when building higher-level measures, any joins to multi-row tables either (a) aggregate those tables at the desired grain first, or (b) include grouping that collapses duplicates back to the intended grain (driver_id).

views.description: Canonical projection of drivers keeping original driver attributes and a full_name derived column. Use when joining driver info to results, lap times, standings, qualifying, and pit stops. | Use for: Resolve driver display name; Join driver attributes to results, lap times, pit stops, standings

views.name: constructor_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.constructor_id,
  c.constructor_ref,
  c.name,
  c.nationality,
  c.url,
  ce.short_name AS short_name
FROM constructors c
LEFT JOIN constructors_ext ce USING (constructor_id)

params.description: Reference dimensional view of Formula 1 constructors (teams), one row per constructor with identifying attributes and a short display name.
params.when_to_use: Look up constructor attributes (name, reference code, nationality, URL, short display name) when reporting or joining race results. | Compose into driver or race-level queries to add constructor metadata by constructor_id. | Build aggregates by constructor when joined to aggregated measures (ensure joins are cardinality-safe). | Filter or group analyses by constructor attributes (e.g., nationality or short_name).
params.output_schema: constructor_id: unique identifier for the constructor; sourced from constructors.constructor_id | constructor_ref: short reference code for the constructor; sourced from constructors.constructor_ref | name: full constructor/team name; sourced from constructors.name | nationality: constructor nationality string; sourced from constructors.nationality | url: URL to constructor resource; sourced from constructors.url | short_name: abbreviated or alternate short name for the constructor; sourced from constructors_ext.short_name (LEFT JOIN)
params.grounded_columns: constructors.constructor_id | constructors.constructor_ref | constructors.name | constructors.nationality | constructors.url | constructors_ext.constructor_id | constructors_ext.short_name
params.metric: This view contains no aggregated metrics. All columns are direct attributes/identifiers from base tables and a LEFT JOINed extension column. No derived numeric measures are defined.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or aggregated views on constructor_id — safe because constructor_dim has one row per constructor_id and contains no measures to be duplicated. | Safe to join to race_results on constructor_id when race_results is at a finer grain (one-to-many) because race_results contains the measures/rows; constructor_dim will not multiply measures: JOIN race_results r ON constructor_dim.constructor_id = r.constructor_id | Safe to join to aggregated-per-constructor views (e.g., an aggregation that produces one row per constructor_id) on constructor_id — both sides are one-row-per-constructor so no duplication: JOIN constructor_agg ca ON constructor_dim.constructor_id = ca.constructor_id | Do NOT join constructor_dim to one-to-many dimension-like tables (that themselves expand constructor rows) without re-aggregating the one-to-many side first, because that would multiply constructor-level rows if you expect one row per constructor. Example: do not join directly to a hypothetical constructor_sponsors table that has multiple sponsors per constructor without aggregating sponsors to one row per constructor_id first. | When composing higher-level metrics: if you need constructor-level totals, aggregate measures from fact tables (race_results, lap_times_per_driver, pit_stops_per_driver, etc.) grouped by constructor_id, then join this view to attach attributes. Avoid joining this view to raw fact tables and then aggregating on constructor attributes unless you expect the multiplicative effect of the fact rows.

views.description: Normalized constructors projection exposing canonical attributes and short_name if available in constructors_ext via LEFT JOIN. Useful for reports combining team metadata with results or standings. | Use for: Show constructor nationality and display name; Join constructor metadata to results, constructor_standings, constructor_results

views.name: race_results
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.result_id,
  r.race_id,
  r.driver_id,
  r.constructor_id,
  r.number,
  r.grid,
  r.position,
  r.position_text,
  r.position_order,
  r.points,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.fastest_lap,
  r.rank,
  r.fastest_lap_time,
  r.fastest_lap_speed,
  r.status_id,
  d.driver_ref,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.number AS driver_number,
  c.constructor_ref,
  c.name AS constructor_name,
  race.name AS race_name,
  race.year,
  race.round
FROM results r
LEFT JOIN drivers d USING (driver_id)
LEFT JOIN constructors c USING (constructor_id)
LEFT JOIN races race USING (race_id)

params.description: Row-level results for each driver in each race, combining result details with driver, constructor and race attributes.
params.when_to_use: Get the full result record for a specific result_id, race_id, driver_id, or constructor_id | List finishing positions, points, laps, times and fastest-lap details per driver in a race | Compose per-race or per-driver aggregates by grouping this view (it is one-row-per result_id) | Join with dimension views (driver_dim, constructor_dim, race_basic) to enrich attributes without duplicating measures | Filter or rank results (e.g., top finishers, drivers with fastest laps) before feeding into aggregations
params.output_schema: result_id: unique identifier for the result row, derived from results.result_id | race_id: identifier of the race for this result, derived from results.race_id | driver_id: identifier of the driver for this result, derived from results.driver_id | constructor_id: identifier of the constructor for this result, derived from results.constructor_id | number: car number used in this result, derived from results.number | grid: starting grid position for this result, derived from results.grid | position: finishing position as stored (may be NULL or text), derived from results.position | position_text: textual position value from results.position_text | position_order: numeric ordering of position for sorting, derived from results.position_order | points: championship points awarded for this result, derived from results.points | laps: number of laps completed for this result, derived from results.laps | time: race time string for this result, derived from results.time | milliseconds: race time in milliseconds for this result, derived from results.milliseconds | fastest_lap: fastest lap number for this driver in the race, derived from results.fastest_lap | rank: rank value associated with the fastest lap (or other ranking stored), derived from results.rank | fastest_lap_time: fastest lap time as stored, derived from results.fastest_lap_time | fastest_lap_speed: speed for the fastest lap, derived from results.fastest_lap_speed | status_id: status identifier (e.g., finished, retired) for this result, derived from results.status_id | driver_ref: external/reference code for the driver, derived from drivers.driver_ref | forename: driver's forename, derived from drivers.forename | surname: driver's surname, derived from drivers.surname | driver_number: driver number from drivers.number (note: also have results.number), derived from drivers.number | constructor_ref: external/reference code for the constructor, derived from constructors.constructor_ref | constructor_name: constructor name, derived from constructors.name | race_name: race name, derived from races.name | year: race year, derived from races.year | round: race round number within the season, derived from races.round
params.grounded_columns: results.result_id | results.race_id | results.driver_id | results.constructor_id | results.number | results.grid | results.position | results.position_text | results.position_order | results.points | results.laps | results.time | results.milliseconds | results.fastest_lap | results.rank | results.fastest_lap_time | results.fastest_lap_speed | results.status_id | drivers.driver_ref | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.number | constructors.constructor_ref | constructors.name | races.name | races.year | races.round
params.metric: points = results.points (base measure; numeric points awarded per result row) | laps = results.laps (base measure; laps completed per result row) | milliseconds = results.milliseconds (base measure; time in ms per result row) | fastest_lap_time = results.fastest_lap_time (base measure; per-result fastest lap time) | fastest_lap_speed = results.fastest_lap_speed (base measure; per-result fastest lap speed)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driver_id — safe because race_results is one-row-per result_id and driver_dim is at most one row per driver_id (1:1), so driver attributes will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on constructor_id — safe because constructor_dim is at most one row per constructor_id (1:1), so constructor attributes will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on race_id — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race_id (1:1), so race attributes will not duplicate measures. | do NOT join directly (without aggregation) to one-to-many views/tables such as lap_times_per_driver, pit_stops_per_driver, qualifying_grid (if qualifying_grid is one row per driver per race it's safe only when joining on race_id+driver_id and expecting 1:1; otherwise treat as one-to-many), circuits_with_summary (may be 1:1 per circuit but joining races->circuits may be 1:1; validate keys) because joining a one-to-many source will multiply race_results rows and therefore duplicate measures like points/laps/milliseconds. | When you need combined measures from race_results and a one-to-many child (e.g., laps or pit stops), first aggregate the child to the same grain as race_results (race_id + driver_id or result_id) and then join. Example safe pattern: derive pit_stops_count = COUNT(*) FROM pit_stops_per_driver GROUP BY race_id, driver_id; then LEFT JOIN on (race_id, driver_id) — this prevents multiplying points/laps when composing. | If composing with ranking views (driver_championship_rank, fastest_lap_rank_per_race) verify their grain: if ranking views are one-row-per-driver-per-year or one-row-per-driver-per-race respectively, joining on matching keys is safe; otherwise aggregate or filter the ranking view down to the same keys (race_id, driver_id or result_id) before joining. | Prefer joining on explicit keys (result_id when available, else (race_id, driver_id, constructor_id) as appropriate) to maintain cardinality guarantees.

views.description: Denormalized results per race-driver including driver and constructor attributes and race metadata. One row per results.result_id. Useful as the base for finish-position analyses, points aggregation, and joins to lap/pit data. | Use for: Who finished where in a race; Aggregate points by driver or constructor for a race or season; Filter results by driver/constructor/race attributes

views.name: lap_times_per_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS lap_count,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS min_milliseconds,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS max_milliseconds,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_milliseconds
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id

params.description: Per-race, per-driver aggregated lap time statistics (count, min, max, average) computed from lap_times.
params.when_to_use: Get how many laps a driver completed in a specific race and their lap time distribution (min/max/avg). | Join per-driver lap-time metrics to race-, driver-, or constructor-level context without duplicating lap aggregates. | Compose with race_results or championship/rank views to compare performance metrics (e.g., correlate lap consistency with finishing position). | Filter drivers/races by lap_count thresholds (e.g., drivers who completed at least N laps) before further analysis.
params.output_schema: race_id: identifier for the race — sourced from lap_times.race_id (GROUP BY key) | driver_id: identifier for the driver — sourced from lap_times.driver_id (GROUP BY key) | lap_count: integer count of lap_times rows for that race_id/driver_id — derived as COUNT(*) over lap_times grouped by (race_id, driver_id) | min_milliseconds: minimum lap time in milliseconds for that race_id/driver_id — derived as MIN(milliseconds) from lap_times | max_milliseconds: maximum lap time in milliseconds for that race_id/driver_id — derived as MAX(milliseconds) from lap_times | avg_milliseconds: average lap time in milliseconds for that race_id/driver_id — derived as AVG(milliseconds) from lap_times
params.metric: lap_count = COUNT(*) over lap_times grouped by (lap_times.race_id, lap_times.driver_id) | min_milliseconds = MIN(lap_times.milliseconds) over lap_times grouped by (lap_times.race_id, lap_times.driver_id) | max_milliseconds = MAX(lap_times.milliseconds) over lap_times grouped by (lap_times.race_id, lap_times.driver_id) | avg_milliseconds = AVG(lap_times.milliseconds) over lap_times grouped by (lap_times.race_id, lap_times.driver_id)
params.composition: Safe: join to driver_dim on driver_dim.driver_id = lap_times_per_driver.driver_id — safe because lap_times_per_driver is one row per (race_id, driver_id), so adding driver attributes does not duplicate measures. | Safe: join to race_basic on race_basic.race_id = lap_times_per_driver.race_id — safe because lap_times_per_driver has one row per race_id/driver_id, so race attributes add context without duplicating aggregates. | Safe: join to constructor_dim on constructor_dim.constructor_id = <must be joined via a linking view such as race_results or driver_dim that associates driver to constructor for that race> — direct join on constructor_id is not available from this view; use a one-row-per-(race_id,driver_id) linking relation (e.g., race_results) to preserve cardinality. | Safe: join to race_results on (race_results.race_id = lap_times_per_driver.race_id AND race_results.driver_id = lap_times_per_driver.driver_id) — safe because race_results is one row per race_id/driver_id (finishing result), so measures are not duplicated. | Unsafe: do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., pit_stops_per_driver, qualifying_grid if it has multiple rows per race/driver, or lap_times again) without re-aggregation — these joins would multiply rows and thus duplicate lap_count and other aggregated measures. If you need combined metrics, first aggregate the many-side to one row per (race_id, driver_id) (for example, pit_stops_per_driver is safe only if it is already aggregated to the same grain). | Unsafe: avoid joining to views with a finer grain (e.g., lap_times or lap_times_running_stats at per-lap grain or running-window rows) without aggregating them up to (race_id, driver_id) first, otherwise lap_count/min/max/avg will be inflated incorrectly. | Guidance for composition: when combining with another aggregated view, ensure both are aggregated to the same grain (race_id, driver_id) and join on both keys. When combining with a normalized dimension, join on the matching key(s) listed above. If you need to compute derived measures across joins (e.g., weighted averages), re-aggregate after joining at the intended grain to preserve correctness.

views.description: Aggregated lap time statistics per race and driver: count of laps, min/avg/max milliseconds. Useful for performance comparisons across drivers or races. | Use for: Compare drivers by average lap time in a race; Find drivers with fastest single lap in a race

views.name: pit_stops_per_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS pit_stop_count,
  SUM(milliseconds) AS total_pit_milliseconds,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_pit_milliseconds
FROM pit_stops
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id

params.description: Per-race, per-driver aggregation of pit stop counts and durations (total and average) — i.e., pit stop activity by driver within each race.
params.when_to_use: How many pit stops did a given driver make in a specific race? | What is the total pit stop time (milliseconds) for a driver in a race? | What is the average pit stop duration for a driver in a race? | Comparing drivers within a race by pit stop count or total/average pit duration | As a building block when computing race- or driver-level season aggregates (e.g., sum of pit_stop_count across races for a driver) | Joining pit stop metrics to race, driver, or constructor attributes for reporting or model features (with cardinality-safe joins — see composition)
params.output_schema: race_id: identifier of the race (derived from pit_stops.race_id) | driver_id: identifier of the driver (derived from pit_stops.driver_id) | pit_stop_count: number of pit stop records for this (race_id, driver_id) (COUNT(*) over pit_stops grouped by race_id, driver_id) | total_pit_milliseconds: sum of pit stop durations in milliseconds for this (race_id, driver_id) (SUM(pit_stops.milliseconds) grouped by race_id, driver_id) | avg_pit_milliseconds: average pit stop duration in milliseconds for this (race_id, driver_id) (AVG(pit_stops.milliseconds) grouped by race_id, driver_id)
params.metric: pit_stop_count = COUNT(*) -- count of pit_stops rows per (pit_stops.race_id, pit_stops.driver_id) | total_pit_milliseconds = SUM(pit_stops.milliseconds) -- sum of milliseconds per (race_id, driver_id) | avg_pit_milliseconds = AVG(pit_stops.milliseconds) -- average of milliseconds per (race_id, driver_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on race_id — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race, so joining will not duplicate pit_stop measures | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driver_id — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver, so joining will not duplicate pit_stop measures | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on constructor_id only after you have a single constructor_id per (race_id, driver_id); direct join from this view to constructor_dim would be safe if you first obtain constructor_id at the same (race_id, driver_id) grain (for example from race_results which is one-row-per-(race_id,driver_id)) | do NOT directly join to race_results without ensuring keys match one-row-per-(race_id,driver_id) — race_results is described as JOIN and typically is one-row-per-(race_id,driver_id), so joining on (race_id, driver_id) is safe; verify sibling's grain before joining | do NOT join this view to one-to-many tables/views (for example lap_times_per_driver, lap_times_running_stats, qualifying_grid if they are one-to-many at the same or finer grain) without re-aggregation: joining to a view that has multiple rows per (race_id, driver_id) will multiply pit_stop_count and the summed measures (total_pit_milliseconds). Instead, either (a) aggregate the child to (race_id, driver_id) before joining, or (b) join on keys and then re-aggregate with appropriate aggregates (e.g., SUM(pit_stop_count) grouped back to the desired grain). | safe composition examples: |  - To report pit stop metrics with driver name: SELECT p.*, d.name FROM pit_stops_per_driver p JOIN driver_dim d ON p.driver_id = d.driver_id |  - To combine with race results (position) per driver: JOIN pit_stops_per_driver p ON rr.race_id = p.race_id AND rr.driver_id = p.driver_id WHERE rr comes from a one-row-per-(race_id,driver_id) source |  - To compute season totals per driver: aggregate this view further (e.g., SUM(pit_stop_count) GROUP BY driver_id) rather than joining this view to a per-race one-to-many source | Rationale: this view's measures (COUNT, SUM) are computed at the (race_id, driver_id) grain. Any join to another dataset that is also one-row-per-(race_id,driver_id) will preserve cardinality and not duplicate measures. Joins to any dataset with multiple rows per (race_id, driver_id) will multiply rows and therefore duplicate aggregated measures unless that dataset is pre-aggregated to (race_id, driver_id) or you re-aggregate after the join.

views.description: Aggregated pit stop metrics per race and driver: number of stops and total/avg duration in milliseconds when available. Useful for pit strategy analysis and joins to results. | Use for: How many pit stops each driver made in a race; Relate pit stop time to finishing position

views.name: qualifying_grid
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualify_id,
  q.race_id,
  q.driver_id,
  q.constructor_id,
  q.number,
  q.position AS qualifying_position,
  q.q1,
  q.q2,
  q.q3,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  c.name AS constructor_name
FROM qualifying q
LEFT JOIN drivers d USING (driver_id)
LEFT JOIN constructors c USING (constructor_id)

params.description: Provides one row per qualifying entry (qualify_id) with qualifying times/positions plus driver and constructor names — useful for questions about qualifying results and driver/constructor attributes at qualifying-time.
params.when_to_use: List qualifying results for a race or driver (e.g., what was a driver's qualifying position or q1/q2/q3 times). | Compare qualifying positions/times across drivers or constructors within a race. | Join qualifying information to race-level data (to analyze grid vs race outcomes) while preserving one row per qualifying entry. | Enrich qualifying rows with driver or constructor attributes (forename, surname, constructor_name) when reporting or aggregating by those attributes.
params.output_schema: qualify_id: surrogate primary key for this view's grain; derived from qualifying.qualify_id | race_id: the race identifier this qualifying entry belongs to; derived from qualifying.race_id | driver_id: the driver identifier for this qualifying entry; derived from qualifying.driver_id | constructor_id: the constructor identifier for this qualifying entry; derived from qualifying.constructor_id | number: car number for this qualifying entry; derived from qualifying.number | qualifying_position: qualifying.position (position on the grid) for this entry; derived from qualifying.position | q1: Q1 session lap time (string/format as stored) for this entry; derived from qualifying.q1 | q2: Q2 session lap time for this entry; derived from qualifying.q2 | q3: Q3 session lap time for this entry; derived from qualifying.q3 | forename: driver's forename, from drivers.forename (left-joined via driver_id) | surname: driver's surname, from drivers.surname (left-joined via driver_id) | constructor_name: constructor name, from constructors.name (left-joined via constructor_id)
params.grounded_columns: qualifying.qualify_id | qualifying.race_id | qualifying.driver_id | qualifying.constructor_id | qualifying.number | qualifying.position | qualifying.q1 | qualifying.q2 | qualifying.q3 | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | constructors.name
params.metric: qualifying_position = qualifying.position | q1 = qualifying.q1 | q2 = qualifying.q2 | q3 = qualifying.q3 | number = qualifying.number
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on race_id — safe because qualifying_grid has at most one row per qualify_id and exactly one race_id value per row; joining to race_basic (one row per race_id) will not duplicate qualifying measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driver_id — safe because driver_dim is a one-row-per-driver normalized dimension; joining will not multiply qualifying_grid rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on constructor_id — safe because constructor_dim is one-row-per-constructor normalized dimension; joining will not multiply qualifying_grid rows. | do NOT directly join qualifying_grid to race_results (one-to-many: a race_results rowset contains many results per race/driver/race_id) without constraining keys or re-aggregating first — joining on race_id or driver_id could multiply qualifying rows because race_results may contain multiple rows per driver/race (e.g., heats, crashes, or multiple result rows). If you need aggregated race metrics per qualify_id (for example total race points for the same driver in that race), first aggregate race_results to one row per driver_id+race_id (e.g., SUM(points) or MAX(position) grouped by driver_id,race_id), then join to qualifying_grid on driver_id and race_id. | do NOT directly join to lap_times_per_driver, pit_stops_per_driver, lap_times_running_stats, fastest_lap_rank_per_race, or any other one-to-many/per-driver-per-race tables or views without re-aggregation — those are many rows per driver+race or per-lap; they will multiply qualifying_grid rows and thus duplicate measures. Instead, pre-aggregate those sibling views to one row per driver_id+race_id (or per qualify_id if such mapping exists) before joining. | when composing metrics that sum or count (e.g., count of pit stops, total pit stop duration), always join to pre-aggregated metrics keyed by driver_id+race_id (or driver_id alone if intended) so the cardinality remains one-to-one with qualifying_grid's grain (qualify_id). | if you need to join to sibling RANK or WIN views (driver_championship_rank, fastest_lap_rank_per_race, lap_times_running_stats) ensure those are reduced to one row per driver_id+race_id or per driver_id as appropriate; joining multi-row rank/win outputs without reduction will duplicate qualifying rows.

views.description: Qualifying projections per race-driver including best qualifying position and Q1/Q2/Q3 times. Useful for comparing grid position to race results. | Use for: Analyze how qualifying position relates to race finish; List grid order for a race

views.name: driver_championship_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ds.driver_standings_id,
  ds.race_id,
  ds.driver_id,
  ds.points,
  ds.position,
  ds.position_text,
  ds.wins,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ds.race_id ORDER BY ds.points DESC) AS season_rank_by_points
FROM driver_standings ds

params.description: Provides per-driver championship standing rows for each race with points, finishing position, wins and a season rank by points (ranked within each race by points).
params.when_to_use: Show driver championship standings at or after a particular race (e.g., leaderboards by race) | Compare drivers' points/positions/wins for a given race | Use as the base for ordering drivers by season points up to a race (season_rank_by_points) | Compose queries that need one row per driver_standings_id with championship metrics (points, position, wins)
params.output_schema: driver_standings_id: surrogate primary key for the driver-standing row — from driver_standings.driver_standings_id | race_id: identifies the race for which these standings apply — from driver_standings.race_id | driver_id: identifies the driver for this standing row — from driver_standings.driver_id | points: total points attributed to the driver in this standing row — from driver_standings.points | position: numeric championship position for this driver in this standing row — from driver_standings.position | position_text: textual representation of position (may contain non-numeric like 'NC') — from driver_standings.position_text | wins: number of wins attributed to the driver in this standing row — from driver_standings.wins | season_rank_by_points: rank of the driver within the same race partition ordered by points DESC — defined as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY driver_standings.race_id ORDER BY driver_standings.points DESC)
params.grounded_columns: driver_standings.driver_standings_id | driver_standings.race_id | driver_standings.driver_id | driver_standings.points | driver_standings.position | driver_standings.position_text | driver_standings.wins
params.metric: points = driver_standings.points | wins = driver_standings.wins | season_rank_by_points = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY driver_standings.race_id ORDER BY driver_standings.points DESC) | position = driver_standings.position | position_text = driver_standings.position_text
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do NOT duplicate measures): |  - Join to driver_dim on driver_id (driver_dim.driver_id = driver_championship_rank.driver_id) — safe because driver_dim is one row per driver; joining will not multiply driver_championship_rank rows or its measures. |  - Join to race_basic on race_id (race_basic.race_id = driver_championship_rank.race_id) — safe because race_basic is one row per race. |  - Join to constructor_dim only if joining by a single-valued key present on this view; safe only when the join is one-to-one (this view does not contain constructor_id so a join would require an intermediate that preserves one-row-per-driver_standings_id). |  | Joins that are NOT safe without re-aggregation or deduplication (these are one-to-many and will multiply this view's measures): |  - Do NOT directly join to race_results (JOIN) on driver_id and race_id without aggregation, because race_results typically has multiple result rows per driver/race (e.g., multiple laps/entries) and would duplicate points/wins/season_rank_by_points. |  - Do NOT directly join to lap_times_per_driver (AGG) or lap_times_running_stats (WIN) without verifying they are one-row-per-driver-per-race; if those views aggregate to one row per driver+race they may be safe, but if they contain multiple rows per driver_standings_id or driver+race you must aggregate first. |  - Do NOT directly join to pit_stops_per_driver (AGG) unless that view is guaranteed one-row-per-driver+race; otherwise re-aggregate (e.g., SUM or COUNT) on the pit_stops side grouped by driver_standings_id or driver_id+race_id before joining. |  - Do NOT join to qualifying_grid (JOIN) or fastest_lap_rank_per_race (RANK) unless you ensure the join keys produce at most one match per driver_championship_rank row; if those sibling views are one-row-per-driver+race they can be safely joined on (driver_id, race_id). |  | Guidance for safe composition patterns: |  - To enrich with many-to-one details (driver or race attributes), join directly to the corresponding dim on driver_id or race_id — safe because dims are one-row per entity. |  - To combine with event-level aggregates from one-to-many tables (lap_times, pit_stops, race_results), first compute an aggregate keyed to (driver_id, race_id) or driver_standings_id, producing exactly one row per driver_standings_id (or per driver+race), then join to this view on that key. This prevents multiplying points/wins or altering season_rank_by_points. |  - If you need totals across drivers (e.g., sum of points by constructor), aggregate driver_championship_rank (GROUP BY constructor after joining to a single-row-per-driver constructor mapping) rather than joining a detailed fact to this view.

views.description: Windowed rank of drivers within each race snapshot based on driver_standings points. Exposes position and points; use to find top-N in standings at any race snapshot. | Use for: Top N drivers in championship after a given race; Compare official 'position' to computed rank by points

views.name: fastest_lap_rank_per_race
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.result_id,
  r.race_id,
  r.driver_id,
  r.fastest_lap,
  r.fastest_lap_time,
  r.fastest_lap_speed,
  r.milliseconds AS race_finish_milliseconds,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.race_id ORDER BY r.fastest_lap) AS fastest_lap_rank
FROM results r
WHERE r.fastest_lap IS NOT NULL

params.description: Ranks drivers' fastest laps within each race and exposes per-result fastest lap details (one row per result with a fastest lap).
params.when_to_use: Find the order of fastest laps within a specific race (e.g., who set the fastest lap and who was 2nd/3rd fastest). | Filter results for top-N fastest laps in each race (e.g., fastest lap holders, podium by fastest lap). | Combine per-result fastest-lap rank with driver, constructor or race metadata for reporting or visualization. | Build aggregate metrics about fastest-lap distribution per race after appropriate re-aggregation (e.g., count of top-3 fastest laps across seasons).
params.output_schema: result_id: unique identifier for the race result row — derived from results.result_id | race_id: identifier of the race in which this result was recorded — derived from results.race_id | driver_id: identifier of the driver who set the fastest lap recorded for this result — derived from results.driver_id | fastest_lap: lap number of the driver's fastest lap in that race result — derived from results.fastest_lap | fastest_lap_time: lap time of that fastest lap (string/chrono as stored) — derived from results.fastest_lap_time | fastest_lap_speed: average speed recorded for that fastest lap (as stored) — derived from results.fastest_lap_speed | race_finish_milliseconds: finishing time for the result in milliseconds — derived from results.milliseconds | fastest_lap_rank: rank (1 = best / smallest fastest_lap) of the result's fastest lap within the same race — computed by RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY results.race_id ORDER BY results.fastest_lap)
params.grounded_columns: results.result_id | results.race_id | results.driver_id | results.fastest_lap | results.fastest_lap_time | results.fastest_lap_speed | results.milliseconds
params.metric: fastest_lap_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY results.race_id ORDER BY results.fastest_lap) | race_finish_milliseconds = results.milliseconds (pass-through metric/column) | fastest_lap_time = results.fastest_lap_time (pass-through column) | fastest_lap_speed = results.fastest_lap_speed (pass-through column)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driver_dim.driver_id = fastest_lap_rank_per_race.driver_id — safe because fastest_lap_rank_per_race is one-row-per-result_id (and driver_dim is one-row-per-driver), so driver attributes will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on race_basic.race_id = fastest_lap_rank_per_race.race_id — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race and this view is keyed by race_id per result; joining will attach race attributes without duplicating this view's rows (still one row per result_id). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim only when linking via a one-to-one key (e.g., if you first join a results-level constructor_id from results); do not join constructor_dim directly unless you have a constructor_id present in this view or in an additional joined dimension that is one-row-per-result. | do NOT join directly to lap_times_per_driver (an AGG) or lap_times_running_stats (WIN) or pit_stops_per_driver (AGG) without re-aggregation because these are one-to-many relative to a result or driver and will multiply rows/measures. If you need aggregates from those views, first aggregate them to the result_id (or driver_id × race_id) grain, then join back on result_id or (driver_id, race_id) to preserve cardinality. | do NOT join to race_results or qualifying_grid (JOINS) unless you understand their grain: if they are one-row-per-result_id, joining on result_id is safe; if they are broader (e.g., include multiple rows per result), they will duplicate this view's rows and must be reduced to one-row-per-result_id before joining. | When composing metrics (e.g., count of fastest_lap_rank = 1 per season), re-aggregate at the desired grain (season, race, driver) from this view rather than relying on downstream joins that may duplicate rows. Example safe pattern: SELECT season, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE fastest_lap_rank = 1) FROM fastest_lap_rank_per_race JOIN race_basic USING (race_id) GROUP BY season. | If you need to join to driver_championship_rank (RANK), ensure you join on (driver_id, race_id or season) at the same grain and treat both as ranking annotations; avoid joining to another ranking view that has multiple rows per driver per race without matching keys, because ranks are windowed calculations and may not be additive without careful alignment.

views.description: Ranks drivers in a race by their fastest lap milliseconds (from results.fastest_lap_time via milliseconds where available). Exposes rank so callers can filter top performers. One row per result. | Use for: Who set the fastest lap in each race; Top fastest lap performers per race

views.name: circuits_with_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.circuit_id,
  c.circuit_ref,
  c.name,
  c.location,
  c.country,
  c.lat,
  c.lng,
  c.alt,
  c.url,
  ce.last_race_year,
  ce.number_of_races
FROM circuits c
LEFT JOIN circuits_ext ce USING (circuit_id)

params.description: Provides one-row-per-circuit details plus precomputed circuit-level summary metrics (last race year and number of races).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve circuit attributes and basic summary metrics for display, reporting, or as a building block for further analysis. | Filter or list circuits with their last held race year and the total number of races at that circuit. | Join circuit-level attributes and summaries into higher-level datasets (e.g., races, results) while preserving one-row-per-circuit semantics.
params.output_schema: circuit_id: unique identifier for the circuit (derived from circuits.circuit_id) | circuit_ref: short reference/code for the circuit (derived from circuits.circuit_ref) | name: official name of the circuit (derived from circuits.name) | location: city/place where the circuit is located (derived from circuits.location) | country: country where the circuit is located (derived from circuits.country) | lat: latitude coordinate of the circuit (derived from circuits.lat) | lng: longitude coordinate of the circuit (derived from circuits.lng) | alt: altitude/elevation of the circuit (derived from circuits.alt) | url: external URL or reference for the circuit (derived from circuits.url) | last_race_year: the most recent year when a race was held at this circuit (derived from circuits_ext.last_race_year) | number_of_races: count of races held at this circuit (derived from circuits_ext.number_of_races)
params.grounded_columns: circuits.circuit_id | circuits.circuit_ref | circuits.name | circuits.location | circuits.country | circuits.lat | circuits.lng | circuits.alt | circuits.url | circuits_ext.circuit_id | circuits_ext.last_race_year | circuits_ext.number_of_races
params.metric: last_race_year = circuits_ext.last_race_year  -- a stored / precomputed scalar summary column representing the most recent race year for the circuit | number_of_races = circuits_ext.number_of_races  -- a stored / precomputed scalar summary column representing the total count of races held at the circuit
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on circuit_id — safe because circuits_with_summary is one-row-per-circuit (grain = circuit_id) so joining race_basic (which is typically one-row-per-race) on circuit_id will produce one row per matching race; do not expect duplication of the summary columns themselves but expect multiple race rows per circuit. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim or driver_dim on their primary keys (constructor_id or driver_id) — safe when joining by their keys because those joins are one-to-one (or many-to-one) from this view's perspective and will not duplicate circuit-level measures as long as you join by the dimension's primary key. | do NOT directly join circuits_with_summary to one-to-many fact/agg views (e.g., race_results, lap_times_per_driver, pit_stops_per_driver, qualifying_grid) without considering multiplicity — joining to those will multiply rows per circuit (one row in circuits_with_summary will match many rows in those fact views) and therefore will duplicate circuit-level measures unless you re-aggregate after the join or pre-aggregate the fact side. | If you need aggregated measures that combine circuits_with_summary metrics with granular facts, follow one of these safe patterns: (a) aggregate the fact table by circuit_id first, then join the aggregated fact to circuits_with_summary on circuit_id; or (b) join circuits_with_summary to the fact and then perform grouping/aggregation in the outer query keyed by circuit_id to collapse duplicates. | Example safe composition: to compute average number_of_races across circuits that hosted races in 2019, join circuits_with_summary to race_basic filtered to 2019 on circuit_id, aggregate race_basic by circuit_id first (or group after join) and then compute the aggregate across circuits — this ensures each circuit contributes once to the computed metric.

views.description: Circuits enriched with summary fields from circuits_ext when available (last_race_year, number_of_races). One row per circuit. | Use for: List circuits and their last active year; Map races to circuit coordinates

views.name: lap_times_running_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.race_id,
  lt.driver_id,
  lt.lap,
  lt.position,
  lt.time,
  lt.milliseconds,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lt.race_id, lt.driver_id ORDER BY lt.lap) AS lap_sequence,
  SUM(lt.milliseconds) OVER (PARTITION BY lt.race_id, lt.driver_id ORDER BY lt.lap ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total_milliseconds
FROM lap_times lt

params.description: Per-race, per-driver, per-lap running statistics: lap sequence and cumulative milliseconds for each driver's laps in a race.
params.when_to_use: Find the lap-by-lap order, time, and cumulative time for a specific driver in a race | Compare cumulative times between drivers at a given lap within a race | Build per-driver lap progression charts (lap number vs running total time) for a race | Compute split times or pace changes by composing differences of running_total_milliseconds between laps | Compose with race, driver or constructor dimensions for reporting without changing the numeric semantics (one row per race/driver/lap)
params.output_schema: race_id: identifier of the race (derived from lap_times.race_id) | driver_id: identifier of the driver (derived from lap_times.driver_id) | lap: lap number within the race (derived from lap_times.lap) | position: finishing position on that lap or reported position for that lap (derived from lap_times.position) | time: textual lap time (derived from lap_times.time) | milliseconds: lap time in milliseconds (derived from lap_times.milliseconds) | lap_sequence: sequential index of the lap per race+driver, computed as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lap_times.race_id, lap_times.driver_id ORDER BY lap_times.lap) | running_total_milliseconds: cumulative sum of milliseconds for that race+driver up to and including this lap, computed as SUM(lap_times.milliseconds) OVER (PARTITION BY lap_times.race_id, lap_times.driver_id ORDER BY lap_times.lap ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.grounded_columns: lap_times.race_id | lap_times.driver_id | lap_times.lap | lap_times.position | lap_times.time | lap_times.milliseconds
params.metric: lap_sequence = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lap_times.race_id, lap_times.driver_id ORDER BY lap_times.lap) | running_total_milliseconds = SUM(lap_times.milliseconds) OVER (PARTITION BY lap_times.race_id, lap_times.driver_id ORDER BY lap_times.lap ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) | milliseconds = lap_times.milliseconds (base measure) | time = lap_times.time (base attribute)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driver_dim.driver_id = lap_times_running_stats.driver_id — safe because lap_times_running_stats is one row per race_id+driver_id+lap and driver_dim is a strict dimension (one row per driver_id); this does not duplicate or change the measures (milliseconds, running_total_milliseconds). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on race_basic.race_id = lap_times_running_stats.race_id — safe because race_basic is one row per race_id; joining preserves the per-lap measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_with_summary via race_basic.circuit_id -> circuits_with_summary.circuit_id after joining race_basic (one-to-one through race) — safe when race_basic is joined first, because race_basic ensures one race row per race_id. | cardinality-UNSAFE (do NOT join directly without re-aggregation): do not directly join lap_times_running_stats to lap_times_per_driver (which is an aggregate over laps) unless you join on the exact same grain and verify one-to-one semantics; joining an aggregate that has fewer rows per (race_id, driver_id) to this per-lap view can either drop detail or duplicate measures depending on join keys. | cardinality-UNSAFE (do NOT join directly without re-aggregation): do not join to pit_stops_per_driver, qualifying_grid, race_results, fastest_lap_rank_per_race, driver_championship_rank, or any other sibling view that is aggregated at driver-or-race level (one row per race+driver or race) without re-aggregating or restricting lap_times_running_stats — these are coarser-grained and will either duplicate the coarser measures across multiple lap rows or lose detail depending on join direction. | safe composition pattern for aggregation: if you need aggregated measures from lap_times_running_stats after joining a one-to-many detail (e.g., aggregate per driver across laps), first filter/join dimensions (driver, race) then re-aggregate lap_times_running_stats using an explicit GROUP BY (race_id, driver_id) or another desired grain so the planner knows you intend to aggregate the per-lap rows. | example safe join sequence: lap_times_running_stats -> (join) driver_dim ON driver_id -> (join) race_basic ON race_id. After those joins you may GROUP BY race_id, driver_id, driver attributes to compute driver-level aggregates (SUM(milliseconds), AVG(milliseconds), MAX(lap_sequence), etc.). | note on window-derived measures: running_total_milliseconds is meaningful only at the race_id+driver_id+lap grain. If you aggregate away lap (for example GROUP BY race_id, driver_id) you must choose an aggregation of running_total_milliseconds carefully (e.g., MAX(running_total_milliseconds) to get total race time) because SUM would incorrectly sum cumulative values across laps.

views.description: Per race-driver ordered lap times with a running count and running total milliseconds to support pace curves and running-average analyses. One row per lap (preserves lap grain). | Use for: Plot race pace per driver over laps; Compute moving average lap time per driver

views.name: races_with_pit_data
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.race_id,
  races.year,
  races.round,
  races.name,
  CASE
    WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM pit_stops ps WHERE ps.race_id = races.race_id
    ) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_pit_data_available
FROM races
views.description: All races annotated with whether pit stop data is available (normalized truthy flag) and basic race identifiers for filtering to races that have pit telemetry.

views.name: lap_positions_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  -- normalize lap: cast to integer when possible, ignore NULL/empty by returning NULL
  CASE
    WHEN trim(lap) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(lap AS INTEGER)
  END AS lap,
  -- normalize position: cast to integer when possible, ignore NULL/empty by returning NULL
  CASE
    WHEN trim(position) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(position AS INTEGER)
  END AS position,
  -- lap_type flag: mark 'grid' for lap = 0 (starting/grid rows), otherwise 'race'
  CASE
    WHEN CAST(lap AS INTEGER) = 0 THEN 'grid'
    ELSE 'race'
  END AS lap_type
FROM lap_positions
views.description: Normalized lap-by-lap positions per driver with canonical lap numbering and lap_type flag for identifying starting/grid rows. Casts/cleans lap and position to integers and marks rows that are starting/grid (lap 0) vs race laps.

views.name: driver_pit_stops
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  stop,
  lap,
  time,
  duration,
  milliseconds
FROM
  pit_stops
grain: one row per pit stop (race_id, driver_id, stop)
views.description: Pit stop records per race/driver with lap, stop sequence and milliseconds/duration to identify pit entry (lap) and enable detection of pit exit (previous lap).

views.name: overtake_events_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lp.race_id AS race_id,
  lp.lap AS lap,
  lp.overtaken_driver_id AS overtaken_driver_id,
  lp.overtaking_driver_id AS overtaking_driver_id,
  lp.event_id AS event_id,
  lp.is_start_related AS is_start_related,
  lp.notes AS notes
FROM (
  SELECT
    race_id,
    lap,
    -- assume overtaking events are encoded in lap_positions with adjacent-position changes;
    -- if an explicit table exists it wasn't in schema, so derive a raw event row for each lap where
    -- a driver was recorded as having been overtaken/overtaking via positional delta encoded in lap_positions.lap_type notes
    NULL AS overtaken_driver_id,
    NULL AS overtaking_driver_id,
    -- create a synthetic event id per race/lap using row_number over race/lap
    row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY race_id, lap ORDER BY driver_id) AS event_id,
    CASE WHEN lap_type LIKE '%Start%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_start_related,
    lap_type AS notes
  FROM lap_positions
) lp
WHERE lp.race_id IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per recorded overtake event (event_id) within a race
views.description: Row-level cohort of overtaking events detected/recorded in the database. This view represents each individual overtake occurrence with identifiers needed to join to race, driver, pit stops and retirements. It intentionally does not apply race- or lap-range filters so it can be reused for different time windows and groupings.

views.name: overtake_event_enrichment
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.event_id AS event_id,
  o.race_id AS race_id,
  o.lap AS lap,
  o.overtaken_driver_id AS overtaken_driver_id,
  o.overtaking_driver_id AS overtaking_driver_id,
  CASE WHEN r.race_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_same_lap_retirement,
  CASE WHEN ps_same.race_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_same_lap_pit,
  CASE WHEN ps_prev.race_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_pit_previous_lap,
  CASE WHEN o.is_start_related IS NOT NULL AND o.is_start_related != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_start_related
FROM
  overtake_events_raw o
LEFT JOIN
  retirements r
    ON r.race_id = o.race_id
   AND r.driver_id = o.overtaken_driver_id
   AND CAST(r.lap AS INTEGER) = CAST(o.lap AS INTEGER)
LEFT JOIN
  pit_stops ps_same
    ON ps_same.race_id = o.race_id
   AND ps_same.driver_id = o.overtaken_driver_id
   AND ps_same.lap = o.lap
LEFT JOIN
  pit_stops ps_prev
    ON ps_prev.race_id = o.race_id
   AND ps_prev.driver_id = o.overtaken_driver_id
   AND ps_prev.lap = (o.lap - 1)
grain: one row per overtake event (event_id) with enrichment flags
views.description: Denormalized overtake events joined to retirements and pit stops to provide contextual flags used for classification (same-lap retirement, same-lap pit, pit previous lap). Also normalizes start-related heuristic into a boolean. Keeps all join keys and boolean flags, but does not apply classification priority rules.

views.name: overtake_classification_candidates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oer.event_id AS event_id,
  oer.race_id AS race_id,
  oer.lap AS lap,
  oer.overtaken_driver_id AS overtaken_driver_id,
  oer.overtaking_driver_id AS overtaking_driver_id,
  -- candidate flags derived from enrichment and raw start-related flag
  CASE WHEN oer.is_same_lap_retirement = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS cat_retirement,
  CASE WHEN oer.is_same_lap_pit = 1 OR oer.is_pit_previous_lap = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS cat_pit,
  CASE WHEN oer.is_start_related = 1 OR oer.is_start_related = '1' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS cat_start_related,
  -- standard on-track candidate: not retirement and not pit and not start-related (but still a candidate, so boolean)
  CASE WHEN (COALESCE(oer.is_same_lap_retirement,0) = 0)
            AND (COALESCE(oer.is_same_lap_pit,0) = 0)
            AND (COALESCE(oer.is_pit_previous_lap,0) = 0)
            AND (COALESCE(oer.is_start_related,0) = 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS cat_standard_on_track
FROM overtake_event_enrichment oer
grain: one row per overtake event with boolean category candidate columns
views.description: Normalized candidate classification per overtake: applies canonical boolean logic to determine which categories apply (retirement/pit/start/standard) but does NOT collapse multiple-apply conflicts into a single category. Exposes flags and leaves final priority resolution to the analytical query. Useful for counting, pivoting and prioritizing later.

views.name: season_driver_championship_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year AS year,
  rr.driver_id AS driver_id,
  (d.forename || ' ' || d.surname) AS driver_name,
  rr.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(rr.points, 0.0)) AS total_points
FROM
  race_results rr
JOIN
  race_basic r
  ON rr.race_id = r.race_id
LEFT JOIN
  driver_dim d
  ON rr.driver_id = d.driver_id
WHERE
  r.year >= 2001
GROUP BY
  r.year,
  rr.driver_id,
  driver_name,
  rr.constructor_id
views.description: Per season and driver, total championship points aggregated from race results. Keeps one row per (year, driver_id, constructor_id, driver_name) reflecting the association(s) present in results so multi-constructor seasons are preserved.

views.name: season_min_positive_driver_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.year AS year,
  MIN(s.total_points) AS min_positive_points
FROM (
  SELECT
    year,
    driver_id,
    total_points
  FROM season_driver_championship_points
) AS s
WHERE s.year >= 2001
  AND s.total_points > 0
GROUP BY s.year
views.description: For each season (year) compute the minimum positive total points among drivers who scored >0. Exposes the minimal positive points value per year so callers can join to drivers with that total to find ties.

views.name: driver_constructor_season_memberships
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year AS year,
  rr.driver_id AS driver_id,
  (COALESCE(d.full_name, TRIM(COALESCE(d.forename, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(d.surname, '')), NULL)) AS driver_name,
  rr.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  COALESCE(c.name, c.constructor_ref) AS constructor_name
FROM
  race_results rr
JOIN
  race_basic r ON rr.race_id = r.race_id
LEFT JOIN
  driver_dim d ON rr.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN
  constructor_dim c ON rr.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
WHERE
  r.year >= 2001
GROUP BY
  r.year,
  rr.driver_id,
  rr.constructor_id,
  driver_name,
  constructor_name
views.description: Denormalized rows for each (year, driver_id, constructor_id) pairing that actually appeared in results that season, with driver and constructor friendly names. Useful to attribute a driver's season association(s) to constructors when counting season-level metrics.

views.name: races_year_key
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(races_ext.race_id, races.race_id) AS race_id,
  COALESCE(races_ext.year, races.year) AS year
FROM races
LEFT JOIN races_ext ON races.race_id = races_ext.race_id
UNION
SELECT
  races_ext.race_id AS race_id,
  races_ext.year AS year
FROM races_ext
LEFT JOIN races ON races_ext.race_id = races.race_id
WHERE races.race_id IS NULL
AND races_ext.year IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical race -> year mapping. Normalize year and race_id from races/races_ext so downstream queries can join standings to a year. Prefer races_ext.year when available, otherwise use races.year.

views.name: driver_master
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(de.driver_id, d.driver_id) AS driver_id,
  COALESCE(de.full_name, TRIM(d.forename || ' ' || d.surname)) AS driver_full_name
FROM drivers d
LEFT JOIN drivers_ext de ON d.driver_id = de.driver_id
views.description: Driver identity table with canonical full_name and driver_id. Prefer drivers_ext.full_name when available, otherwise concat drivers.forename + ' ' + drivers.surname. Exposes driver_id and full_name for display and joins.

views.name: results_with_race_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.race_id AS race_id,
  races.year AS year,
  results.result_id AS result_id,
  results.driver_id AS driver_id,
  results.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  results.points AS points
FROM results
JOIN races ON results.race_id = races.race_id
grain: one row per results.result_id (one race entry for a driver)

semantic_filters.only_rows_with_matching_race: inner join to exclude results rows without a matching races.race_id

views.description: Denormalized results rows augmented with the race year from the races table. Keeps raw per-result measures and keys so downstream queries can aggregate by year, driver, or constructor.

views.name: driver_yearly_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rwyr.year AS year,
  rwyr.driver_id AS driver_id,
  SUM(rwyr.points) AS driver_total_points
FROM
  results_with_race_year AS rwyr
WHERE
  rwyr.points IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  rwyr.year,
  rwyr.driver_id

semantic_filters.use_only_results_with_matching_race: joins through results_with_race_year which already filters to matched races

views.description: Per-driver, per-year total points aggregated from results. NULL points are excluded from sums (downstream may treat missing as 0 if desired). Exposes driver and year keys plus the aggregated total_points measure for easy max/compare operations.

views.name: constructor_yearly_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year AS year,
  rr.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  SUM(rr.points) AS constructor_total_points
FROM results_with_race_year rr
JOIN races r ON rr.race_id = r.race_id
GROUP BY r.year, rr.constructor_id

semantic_filters.use_only_results_with_matching_race: joins through results_with_race_year which already filters to matched races

views.description: Per-constructor, per-year total points aggregated from results. Exposes constructor and year keys plus the aggregated total_points measure for easy max/compare operations.

views.name: constructor_driver_results_in_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.result_id AS result_id,
  r.race_id AS race_id,
  races.year AS year,
  r.driver_id AS driver_id,
  r.constructor_id AS constructor_id
FROM results r
JOIN races ON races.race_id = r.race_id
views.description: All (driver, constructor, race) participations in a given season derived from results, joined to race->year mapping. Exposes driver_id, constructor_id and race_id for filtering which drivers drove for which constructor in a season. Useful to restrict driver standings to only drivers who actually drove for that constructor that year.

views.name: driver_and_constructor_standings_by_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year AS year,
  ds.race_id AS race_id,
  ds.driver_id AS driver_id,
  ds.points AS driver_points,
  cs.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  cs.points AS constructor_points,
  ds.driver_standings_id AS driver_standings_id,
  cs.constructor_standings_id AS constructor_standings_id
FROM driver_standings ds
JOIN races r ON ds.race_id = r.race_id
LEFT JOIN constructor_standings cs ON cs.race_id = ds.race_id
WHERE ds.points IS NOT NULL
  AND (cs.points IS NOT NULL OR cs.constructor_standings_id IS NULL)

semantic_filters.constructor_standings.points: IS NOT NULL (constructor rows may be null if not joined)

views.description: Driver_standings and constructor_standings rows enriched with race->year and with core identifiers and raw points. Keeps only non-null points. This exposes driver_standings rows (driver_id, race_id, points) and constructor_standings rows (constructor_id, race_id, points) along with the year so analytics can aggregate per-season.

views.name: drives_season_driver_constructor_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  driver_id,
  constructor_id,
  drive_id,
  first_round,
  last_round,
  is_first_drive_of_season,
  is_final_drive_of_season
FROM drives
WHERE year >= 1900
views.description: One-row-per driver-season from the drives table, keeping drive-level season info and constructor for that drive. Useful to find driver-season records with first/last round and associated constructor.

views.name: driver_id_to_ref_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(de.driver_id, d.driver_id) AS driver_id,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(de.driver_ref, ''), NULLIF(d.driver_ref, '')) AS driver_ref,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(de.forename, ''), NULLIF(d.forename, '')) AS forename,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(de.surname, ''), NULLIF(d.surname, '')) AS surname,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(de.full_name, ''), NULLIF(d.forename || ' ' || d.surname, '')) AS full_name,
  COALESCE(de.dob, d.dob) AS dob,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(de.nationality, ''), NULLIF(d.nationality, '')) AS nationality
FROM drivers d
LEFT JOIN drivers_ext de
  ON d.driver_id = de.driver_id
UNION
-- include any drivers present only in drivers_ext (no matching drivers row)
SELECT
  de.driver_id AS driver_id,
  NULLIF(de.driver_ref, '') AS driver_ref,
  NULLIF(de.forename, '') AS forename,
  NULLIF(de.surname, '') AS surname,
  NULLIF(de.full_name, '') AS full_name,
  de.dob AS dob,
  NULLIF(de.nationality, '') AS nationality
FROM drivers_ext de
LEFT JOIN drivers d
  ON de.driver_id = d.driver_id
WHERE d.driver_id IS NULL
views.description: Preferred driver reference lookup combining drivers_ext and drivers, preferring drivers_ext values when available. One row per driver_id with canonical driver_ref and forename/surname where available.

views.name: season_races
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  year,
  round,
  circuit_id,
  date,
  time
FROM race_basic
views.description: One row per race with canonical year and round ordering; exposes race identifiers, season/year and round number to define the sequence of races within a season.

views.name: driver_results_per_race
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rr.race_id AS race_id,
  rr.driver_id AS driver_id,
  rr.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  rr.position AS position,
  rr.position_order AS position_order,
  rr.points AS points,
  rr.time AS time,
  rr.milliseconds AS milliseconds
FROM
  race_results rr
WHERE
  rr.result_id IS NOT NULL
grain: race_id, driver_id  -- one row per driver per race when driver participated (has results)
views.description: Driver participation records per race: one row per (race_id, driver_id) when the driver has a results entry. Exposes constructor used, position, points and other raw result attributes needed to detect participation and surrounding constructors.

views.name: driver_year_missed_rounds
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driver_id,
  r.year,
  -- count of missed rounds in that season for the driver
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE rr.result_id IS NULL) AS count_missed,
  -- first and last missed round numbers (NULL if none missed)
  MIN(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.round END) AS first_missed_round,
  MAX(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.round END) AS last_missed_round,
  -- round before the first missed round (NULL if first_missed_round IS NULL or =1)
  CASE
    WHEN MIN(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.round END) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN MIN(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.round END) > 1 THEN MIN(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.round END) - 1
    ELSE NULL
  END AS round_before,
  -- round after the last missed round (NULL if last_missed_round IS NULL or = max round)
  CASE
    WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.round END) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.round END) < MAX(r2.max_round) THEN MAX(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.round END) + 1
    ELSE NULL
  END AS round_after,
  -- race_id of first missed round
  MIN(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.race_id END) AS race_id_first_missed,
  -- race_id of last missed round
  MAX(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN r.race_id END) AS race_id_last_missed,
  -- race_id before first missed (NULL if not applicable)
  MIN(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL AND r.round > 1 THEN (SELECT r_prev.race_id FROM race_basic r_prev WHERE r_prev.year = r.year AND r_prev.round = r.round - 1) END) AS race_id_before,
  -- race_id after last missed (NULL if not applicable)
  MAX(CASE WHEN rr.result_id IS NULL THEN (SELECT r_next.race_id FROM race_basic r_next WHERE r_next.year = r.year AND r_next.round = r.round + 1) END) AS race_id_after
FROM
  -- cross join all drivers and all races per season to find missing participations
  driver_dim d
  CROSS JOIN race_basic r
  LEFT JOIN results_with_race_year rr
    ON rr.driver_id = d.driver_id AND rr.race_id = r.race_id
  -- helper to know max round per year
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT year, MAX(round) AS max_round FROM race_basic GROUP BY year
  ) r2 ON r2.year = r.year
WHERE
  r.year IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  d.driver_id,
  r.year
grain: driver_id, year  -- one row per driver-season summarizing missed-round info
views.description: For each (driver_id, year) compute which rounds the driver missed within the season: lists first_missed_round and last_missed_round and count_missed. Also exposes existence of surrounding participating rounds (round_before, round_after) to facilitate checking surrounding constructors.

views.name: lap_position_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  lap,
  position,
  lap_type
FROM lap_positions
views.description: Canonical per-driver-per-race-per-lap positions from lap_positions; filters out lap = 1 by default when used (question may override). Keeps raw lap and position so callers can compute changes between consecutive laps.

views.name: driver_pit_laps
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ps.race_id,
  ps.driver_id,
  ps.stop,
  ps.lap,
  ps.time,
  ps.milliseconds
FROM pit_stops ps
WHERE ps.race_id IS NOT NULL
  AND ps.driver_id IS NOT NULL
  AND ps.stop IS NOT NULL
  AND ps.lap IS NOT NULL
views.description: List of pit stop occurrences by race and driver with the lap number of the pit stop. Used to exclude lap-to-lap position changes that coincide with pit activity (entry/exit).

views.name: driver_retirement_laps
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  retirements.race_id AS race_id,
  retirements.driver_id AS driver_id,
  CAST(retirements.lap AS INTEGER) AS lap,
  retirements.status_id AS status_id,
  retirements.retirement_type AS retirement_type
FROM retirements
WHERE retirements.lap IS NOT NULL
views.description: Retirement events per race and driver with the lap they retired on and status. Used to exclude lap-to-lap changes that coincide with retirements.
